narrative.title: The Signal Gate Bench Test
narrative.scenario: A hardware lab certifies three micro-operations on its logic probe: a difference-flip between two signal words (XOR), a read of one bit position, and a write that switches a bit on. Each probe routine runs in constant time and is exercised with concrete word values before sign-off.
narrative.inputFormat: Integers a, b for the XOR test; c (bit index), d (word) for the read test; e (bit index), f (word) for the write test.
narrative.outputFormat: Return a triple: a XOR b; then 1 if bit c of d is set else 0; then f with bit e forced on.
constraints: all operations must run in O(1)

testCases.explanation: 5^3 = 6; bit 1 of 6 (110) is 1; 8 with bit 0 set becomes 9.
12^10 = 6 (1100 vs 1010 differ in two bits); bit 0 of 4 is unset; forcing bit 1 on gives 4 | 2 = 6.

hintLevels: Level 1: Three primitives: ^ flips differing bits, >> n moves bit n to position 0, | with a one-hot mask forces a bit on.
Level 2: Reading bit c is (d >> c) & 1; writing is f | (1 << e), which is harmless when the bit is already set.
Level 3: No branching is needed anywhere — all three answers are single expressions.
